newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-SHOWDOWNS FOR THE FORMULA ONE DRIVERS' TITLE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SHOWDOWNS FOR THE FORMULA ONE DRIVERS' TITLE.

text.p: Britain's Damon Hill and Canada's Jacques Villeneuve clash in the final Grand Prix of the season in Suzuka, Japan, on Sunday for the Formula One world drivers' title.
The following is an analysis of the showdown races which have settled the championship over the last 10 years:
1986 - Australian Grand Prix at Adelaide

Briton Nigel Mansell was thwarted in his bid to win the title for the first time in his Williams by a dramatic tyre blowout. This allowed Frenchman Alain Prost to win the race for McLaren and claim his second title. Prost finished with 72 points to Mansell's 70.
1987 - Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka
Mansell crashed in practice and was injured. He could not take part in the race, allowing Williams team mate Brazilian Nelson Piquet to win his third world championship. Piquet 73 points, Mansell 61.
1988 - Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka

Again the championship was settled in the penultimate race with Brazilian Ayrton Senna winning in a McLaren ahead of his team mate and only title rival Prost. Senna took the title with 90 points to Prost's 87 thanks to a brilliant drive in wet conditions.
1989 - Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka

Prost took the title after a stormy race in which he collided with his McLaren team mate Senna at the chicane. The Brazilian, who restarted with a push and finished first, was disqualifed for missing the chicane and for accepting illegal assistance. Prost, who did not finish the race, criticised Senna but took the title by 76 to 60. Italian Alessandro Nannini was declared race winner for Benetton, his only Grand Prix victory.
1990 - Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka

Senna, who claimed Prost had crashed deliberately and cheated to claim the title the previous year, exacted revenge by smashing the Frenchman's Ferrari off the track with his McLaren at the first corner before going on to take the title. Later, he ranted at length about the 1989 race during a winner's speech littered with profanities. He accused the sport's governing body of assisting Prost. Piquet won the race for Benetton. Senna 78 points, Prost 71.
1991 - Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka
Senna again, but this time after finishing second to his McLaren team mate Gerhard Berger of Austria, whom he allowed past to win the race. Senna 96 points, Mansell 72.
1992 - Hungarian Grand Prix at Budapest

Senna won the race. Mansell, in a car equipped with computerised active suspension, finished second and took the title at last from Williams team mate Riccardo Patrese of Italy. Mansell 108 points, Patrese 56.
1993 - Portuguese Grand Prix at Estoril

Prost, in a Williams, announced his impending retirement 48 hours before the race and then finished second to a young Michael Schumacher of Germany, who claimed his second race victory for Benetton. Prost took his fourth and final title with 99 points from Senna's 73.
1994 - Australian Grand Prix at Adelaide

The last occasion the title was decided on the final day. Schumacher, in a Benetton, started just a point ahead of his only rival Hill in a Williams. A sensational race decided by a collision when Schumacher turned into Hill after 35 of the 81 laps. Both cars were damaged and out, and Schumacher was champion. Mansell won the race, his last victory in Formula One. Schumacher 92 points, Hill 91.
1995 - Pacific Grand Prix at Aida, Japan
A brilliant win by dominant Schumacher, driving a Benetton, sealed the title from Hill, who finished third in the race. Schumacher 102 points, Hill 69.
